title: The help system
summary: Where the help button gets its text, what it sends over the internet, and how to turn the internet part off.
html:
The question mark in the header opens the documentation for the screen you are on. This page explains where that text comes from, because the honest answer matters to anyone running this on a private network.

Where the text comes from, in order

  1. A copy fetched recently — anything read in the last week is reused.
  2. The copy that shipped in your download. Every article is included in the files you uploaded. Help works with the network cable pulled out.
  3. The documentation site, if it can be reached, to pick up anything written since your release.
  4. The copy that shipped, again, if the site cannot be reached.

You are never shown a spinner that ends in nothing. There is always text.

What leaves your server

When an article is opened — and only then, never when a page loads — your server makes one request:

GET https://docs.ultimateclientmanager.com/api/v1/<article>.json?v=3.5&lang=en

That is the whole of it. Three things: which article, which major version of this software, and a language code.

It carries no licence or purchase code, no web address or domain or IP for your installation, no user name or email, and nothing at all about your customers, invoices or jobs. There is no installation identifier, anonymous or otherwise.

Two details are worth stating because they are the ones that are usually got wrong:

  • Your browser never makes this request. Your server does. A request your browser does not make cannot carry a Referer or an Origin header, and those headers are how an installation's address usually escapes without anyone intending it.
  • The article name is checked against the list included in your download before any address is built. An article that is not on that list is answered locally and no request is made.

This has not always been true

Until recently the help button opened a frame on a third party site with this installation's purchase codes and web address in the address bar, on every admin page load. That is gone, the code that did it is removed, and the design above exists specifically so it cannot come back by accident. There is a test in the build that asserts the exact address above, so adding a fourth field to it fails the build.

Turning the internet part off

Settings → Help → untick Fetch the latest documentation.

With that off, the copy in your download is the only source and this installation makes no outbound request for help, ever. That is the right setting for an air-gapped or closed-network installation.

If you leave it on and there is no route out, nothing hangs: requests give up after a few seconds, and after three failures in a row the system stops trying for an hour rather than retrying on every click.

Who can see help

By default anyone whose role allows it. If you would rather restrict it, tick Only show help menu for Super Administrator.

On installations upgraded from an older version that restriction is already on, because it used to be the default — which meant only the very first user account ever saw the help button. Untick it to let your staff read the documentation for the screen they are on. See Staff and permissions.
